I read the whole script. It's 8 lines and about 36 seconds, so you'll end up using 1–2 ideas per line. Each line below has the meaning I'm cutting to, 3 B-roll ideas and 3 animation ideas. ★ marks my pick. Everything uses real, named footage or assets, with no stock.

---

### 1. "Hey, it's Kristina Shea, and welcome to The Kristina Shea Show."
**Meaning:** introduce her as someone worth listening to. Keep her on camera for most of this line.

**B-roll**
- ★ Her own footage: Kristina on a stage or hosting a WomenUp event, pulled from her LinkedIn, Instagram or YouTube.
- Behind the scenes from the 14 Nov shoot: lights going on and her sitting down, so it feels like the show is opening its doors.
- Start on the wide camera angle and cut to the mid angle on "The Kristina Shea Show".

**Animation**
- ★ Her name types on beside her, aligned to the side it sits on. "KRISTINA SHEA" bold with a small "Host" line underneath. It fades in and stays.
- A scan of her real signature writes itself on, then becomes the show logo.
- A real camera-monitor overlay with a REC dot "goes live" on "welcome", then falls away.

### 2. "AI meets ambition and impact, powered by WomenUp."
**Meaning:** the show is where technology meets human drive, and a women's community backs it.

**B-roll**
- ★ Women on real AI stages: Mira Murati presenting GPT-4o (May 2024), Lisa Su holding up AMD's chip at CES, Fei-Fei Li's TED talk.
- WomenUp's own footage of events and members, with their logo on stage.
- Cut on the three words: **AI** = chip or keynote, **ambition** = founder moment, **impact** = WomenUp crowd.

**Animation**
- ★ "AI" types on in a mono font with a cursor, "ambition" lands in serif, and "impact" punches in bold. The three words slide together and the real WomenUp logo appears under "powered by".
- "Meets" as a collision: a real chip photo from the left and a real photo of a woman leader from the right meet in the centre with a light flash that reveals the logo.
- Power-on: the frame starts dim, then the WomenUp logo glows on and lights the shot, with a light sweep on "powered by".

### 3. "We're going behind the scenes of success, exploring the ambition, decisions, and the defining moments that shape leaders and change makers."
**Meaning:** the show reveals what sits under polished success: the hard calls. This is the longest line (about 8 s), so it can take 2–3 shots.

**B-roll**
- ★ The Situation Room photo (Pete Souza, May 2011), the most famous "behind the decision" image. Push in slowly.
- Whitney Wolfe Herd ringing the Nasdaq bell with her son on her hip at the Bumble IPO (2021), a defining moment for a female founder.
- Oprah's first *AM Chicago* episode (1984) cut against her later stage footage: the unseen early chapter.
- Her own BTS for the words "behind the scenes": makeup, slate, crew.

**Animation**
- ★ Magazine tear: a real Forbes or TIME cover of a leader fills the frame, then a real paper-tear texture rips it open to show raw BTS footage behind it.
- Contact sheet: a real photographer's proof sheet slides in. On "defining moments" a red grease-pencil circle draws around one frame, and we push into that frame as it becomes footage.
- Timeline: real photo cards of one leader at different ages slide along a line, with AMBITION / DECISIONS / DEFINING MOMENTS stamped on them. "Leaders" sits left-aligned and "change makers" right-aligned.

### 4. "Let's talk about the future of work, leadership, and society itself."
**Meaning:** the conversation grows from your desk to the whole world.

**B-roll**
- Work: Figure's humanoid robot working on BMW's Spartanburg line (2024).
- Leadership: the world-leader group photo from the Bletchley Park AI Safety Summit (Nov 2023), or the Davos stage.
- ★ Society: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva saying AI will affect almost 40% of jobs (Jan 2024), with the news footage and headline.

**Animation**
- ★ Zoom out in Google Earth Studio: office building (**work**), then the city (**leadership**), then the globe (**society**). Each word lands at its level.
- Three real paper file tabs labelled WORK / LEADERSHIP / SOCIETY pull out one per word.
- Real headlines about AI and jobs stack up as paper clippings, with the key words highlighted.

### 5. "Because AI isn't just changing tools, it's changing power."
**Meaning:** AI is shifting who holds power, not just which software we use. This is the strongest line of the trailer.

**B-roll**
- ★ Tech CEOs seated up front at the Jan 2025 inauguration (Musk, Bezos, Zuckerberg, Pichai). It's the clearest picture of tech becoming power.
- The Stargate announcement at the White House (Jan 2025): Trump with Altman, Son and Ellison.
- Sam Altman sworn in at the Senate hearing (May 2023), or Jensen Huang holding up the Blackwell chip at GTC 2024.

**Animation**
- ★ "TOOLS" appears next to a real hammer or wrench cut-out and gets struck through. "POWER" lands bold with a gold glow over the inauguration photo.
- Chess promotion: a real pawn slides up a real board and becomes a queen on "power", which also nods to women in leadership.
- A market-cap bar race using Nvidia's real numbers: $1T in 2023 to $4T+ in 2025, passing the old giants.

### 6. "So the question is, are you leading it or watching it happen?"
**Meaning:** shape the change, or be shaped by it.

**B-roll**
- ★ Steve Jobs unveiling the iPhone (Jan 2007) against Steve Ballmer laughing at it on TV the same year.
- Kodak: Steve Sasson's 1975 digital camera prototype, then Kodak's 2012 bankruptcy headline. They invented it and watched it happen.
- A real keynote crowd filming on their phones while one person leads on stage.

**Animation**
- Split screen: Jobs on the left with "LEADING" left-aligned, Ballmer on the right with "WATCHING" right-aligned. Wipe on "or", then land on Kristina for the question.
- ★ Meta pull-back: on "watching it happen" the camera pulls back to show this trailer playing on a phone in someone's hand. The viewer is the watcher.
- "LEADING IT" and "WATCHING IT HAPPEN" stacked, with a real cursor hovering between them that never clicks, so the question stays open.

### 7. "And if this sparks something in you, lean in."
**Meaning:** an invitation. If something lit up, step forward.

**B-roll**
- The Paris 2024 Olympic cauldron being lit (Marie-José Pérec and Teddy Riner): a real spark moment.
- Sheryl Sandberg's 2010 TED talk, where "lean in" started. She's polarising, so check with the client first.
- ★ Her own footage: Kristina leaning toward the camera, or a WomenUp member stepping up to a mic.

**Animation**
- A real ember or film-burn overlay drifts in on "sparks" and lights "LEAN IN" gold from left to right.
- ★ A slow push-in anchored on her face on "lean in", so the camera leans in with her. Cut to the tightest of the three angles.
- A light-leak bloom on "sparks" carries the cut into her close-up.

### 8. "You're part of the conversation now."
**Meaning:** the viewer is inside the show now, not outside it.

**B-roll**
- ★ The empty chair across from her in the studio, from the wide angle or a quick extra shot. The seat is for "you".
- A real WomenUp audience member taking the mic, or applause.
- The real comment section on her posts, scrolling.

**Animation**
- Real chat bubbles: her line, then a "…" typing indicator from "you".
- A real paper tent card on the studio table reading "YOU", across from her.
- ★ End card: show logo, "powered by WomenUp" and a follow prompt, with her voice waveform splitting into two (hers and the viewer's) to show a conversation.

# PDF Processing Guide

## Overview

This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.

## Quick Start

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Read a PDF
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")

# Extract text
text = ""
for page in reader.pages:
    text += page.extract_text()
```

## Python Libraries

### pypdf - Basic Operations

#### Merge PDFs
```python
from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader

writer = PdfWriter()
for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
    for page in reader.pages:
        writer.add_page(page)

with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

#### Split PDF
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    writer = PdfWriter()
    writer.add_page(page)
    with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
```

#### Extract Metadata
```python
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
meta = reader.metadata
print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
```

#### Rotate Pages
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

page = reader.pages[0]
page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
writer.add_page(page)

with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction

#### Extract Text with Layout
```python
import pdfplumber

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for page in pdf.pages:
        text = page.extract_text()
        print(text)
```

#### Extract Tables
```python
with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for j, table in enumerate(tables):
            print(f"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:")
            for row in table:
                print(row)
```

#### Advanced Table Extraction
```python
import pandas as pd

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    all_tables = []
    for page in pdf.pages:
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for table in tables:
            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
                all_tables.append(df)

# Combine all tables
if all_tables:
    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
    combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
```

### reportlab - Create PDFs

#### Basic PDF Creation
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
width, height = letter

# Add text
c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")

# Add a line
c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)

# Save
c.save()
```

#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
story = []

# Add content
title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
story.append(title)
story.append(Spacer(1, 12))

body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
story.append(body)
story.append(PageBreak())

# Page 2
story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))

# Build PDF
doc.build(story)
```

#### Subscripts and Superscripts

**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉, ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.

Instead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:
```python
from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

styles = getSampleStyleSheet()

# Subscripts: use <sub> tag
chemical = Paragraph("H<sub>2</sub>O", styles['Normal'])

# Superscripts: use <super> tag
squared = Paragraph("x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>", styles['Normal'])
```

For canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.

## Command-Line Tools

### pdftotext (poppler-utils)
```bash
# Extract text
pdftotext input.pdf output.txt

# Extract text preserving layout
pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt

# Extract specific pages
pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5
```

### qpdf
```bash
# Merge PDFs
qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf

# Split pages
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf

# Rotate pages
qpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees

# Remove password
qpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf
```

### pdftk (if available)
```bash
# Merge
pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf

# Split
pdftk input.pdf burst

# Rotate
pdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf
```

## Common Tasks

### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs
```python
# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image
import pytesseract
from pdf2image import convert_from_path

# Convert PDF to images
images = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')

# OCR each page
text = ""
for i, image in enumerate(images):
    text += f"Page {i+1}:\n"
    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
    text += "\n\n"

print(text)
```

### Add Watermark
```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Create watermark (or load existing)
watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]

# Apply to all pages
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    page.merge_page(watermark)
    writer.add_page(page)

with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### Extract Images
```bash
# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)
pdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix

# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.
```

### Password Protection
```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    writer.add_page(page)

# Add password
writer.encrypt("userpassword", "ownerpassword")

with open("encrypted.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

## Quick Reference

| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |
|------|-----------|--------------|
| Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |
| Split PDFs | pypdf | One page per file |
| Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |
| Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |
| Create PDFs | reportlab | Canvas or Platypus |
| Command line merge | qpdf | `qpdf --empty --pages ...` |
| OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |
| Fill PDF forms | pdf-lib or pypdf (see FORMS.md) | See FORMS.md |

def _word_state(t, t_in, t_out):
    """entry/exit progress of one word -> (opacity, blur px, x offset, h-stretch)"""
    if t < t_in: return None
    e = EASE_OUT3((t-t_in)*FPS/IN_F)
    op, bl, dx, st = e, 26*(1-e), 22*(1-e), 0.22*(1-e)
    if t_out is not None and t >= t_out:
        x = EASE_IO((t-t_out)*FPS/OUT_F)
        if x >= 1: return None
        op *= 1-x; bl += 26*x; dx -= 18*x; st += 0.18*x
    return op, bl, dx, st

def _line_layout(words, px):

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-11-20 13:45

Scenes 02 and 03 are rebuilt, and their four stills are open in Preview. The PDF and the Photos album are updated too.

**Scene 03, "powered by WomenUp":**
- **Photos:** eight iconic photos of women rising sit on an aligned grid, four on top and four below:
  - Rosie "We Can Do It!", the 1913 suffrage procession and the 2017 Women's March.
  - Malala, Katherine Johnson and Sally Ride.
  - Ruth Bader Ginsburg and Marie Curie.
- **Centre bar:** in the middle is a glowing bar exactly as wide as the grid. "powered by" sits on top, and the WomenUp logo arrives with the glowing pixel wipe from top to bottom.
- **Highlight:** the photos dim as the logo lands so it stands out.
- **Stills:** one mid-wipe (03a) and one with the logo landed (03b).
- **Alignment:** every photo is the same size with the same gaps, the bar matches the grid's edges, and the text is centred.
- **The logo:** WomenUp has no separate logo file anywhere; Kristina's site only writes "WomenUp™" as text. I cut the official wordmark ("Women Up / AI / Ambition + Impact") cleanly off their signup banner. If Kristina has a proper logo file, I'll swap it in.
- **The photos:** "famous photos of WomenUp" could mean photos of WomenUp itself, but it's brand new and has none. So I used famous photos of women rising instead. If you meant something else, tell me.

**Scene 02, "AI meets ambition and impact":**
- **Shots:**
  - 02a is the 24:35 shot, with "AI meets" over a neon box saying "ambition".
  - 02b cuts to the 25:05 wide of the stage with the "+21%" chart, and the box retypes to "and impact".
- **Pacing:** the line is about 2 s, so it's two shots of about a second each. A third shot would feel rushed.
- **Two catches on the 24:35 shot:**
  - The chip she's holding up falls outside the vertical crop, because it's too far from her face to fit both in 9:16.
  - The keynote video has black bars, so the shot is enlarged and a bit soft.

def finish(img, seed=0, vig=0.30):
    """graphics finish from the skill: grain + vignette"""
    img = J.grain(img, 5.0, seed)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:J.H, 0:J.W].astype(np.float32)
    r = np.sqrt(((xx - J.W / 2) / (J.W * 0.62)) ** 2 + ((yy - J.H / 2) / (J.H * 0.55)) ** 2)
    img = img * (1 - vig * np.clip(r - 0.35, 0, 1) ** 1.4)[..., None]
    return np.clip(img, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def save(img, name):
    p = os.path.join(OUT, name + '.png')
    Image.fromarray(finish(img)).save(p)

# Jennifer Musselman style

A vertical reel (1080x1920, 29.97 fps) of a speaker, copied from Krish's reference `~/Krish works/samples/jennifer musselman_TH_001.mp4` (AE project `~/Project files/Jennifer musselman_TH_001.aep`). The full frame-by-frame study is `refs/STUDY.md`; key frames `refs/keys.jpg`; cut list `refs/cuts.json`. **Nothing from the documentry or flourish skills** (different style), but every global edit rule in memory still applies (cut silence/fillers, no third-person voices, safe zone, no text on faces, ask before rendering, open the render, music -35 to -38 LUFS instrumental).

## v2 LOOK (2026-11-18, Krish: "match these 3 reels perfectly") -- THIS OVERRIDES the v1 look below
Refs: 3 Composio "Agents at Work" reels (IG Dd4rKXERLnC, Dcy1LtuhIfl, DccbZ38RO7M; local copies `~/ks-ron-build/refs_jen2/dl/`).
Full frame-by-frame study with measured colours, timings and motion curves: `refs2/STUDY2.md` (tools in `refs2/tools/`: sheet.py, motion.py).
Engine: `scripts2/jstyle2.py` (captions, TechBG, typed_word, neon_box, panel, card, glass_card, persp, halftone), `scripts2/render2.py`, `scripts2/plan2.py`.
- Font: Instrument Serif (+Italic) drawn 15 % wider (`~/ks-ron-build/reel2/fonts/`). Mono (Menlo) only for data rows / 01 grid.
- Captions: centre-aligned 2-line block in the empty space beside the head (never on a face/person); small lead line + main line on a
  50 % black box that appears at full width before its first word; words enter one by one (6 frames: fade, h-blur 26->0, slide 22 px, stretch);
  the lead leaves word by word when the main line is under way; main words too wide for the column move up to the lead (lead wraps, never shrinks).
- Palette: black ground 5-16, teal (33,200,154) / cyan (40,250,242) -> blue (5,40,167); white type. Gradients always teal top-left -> blue bottom-right.
- Graphics on the black tech ground ("01" glyph grid in drifting soft patches, number rows, binary strip, grey glitch blocks): type-on big
  serif word with blue raised newest letter + glowing cursor bar; gradient serif word; dark panel with segmented teal->blue bar; photo collage
  with thin light borders; card carousel (gradient squares + dark cards, mosaic reveal); 3D grey numeral + neon gradient box; glass code card
  rotating in from 3D + grey word typing behind + white label pill with scrambled letters; big glowing serif word over colour B-roll.
- Transitions: halftone dot transition (0.5 s, blocky) speaker -> graphic / B-roll; graphic -> speaker = hard cut + 2 frames B&W + 3-frame colour return
  + ONE ease-out zoom-out 1.052 -> 1.0 over 1.1 s (measured). Same-person cuts: locked, 5-frame blend.
- Glass code card = a ROTATION TRANSITION (Krish 2026-11-19): enters huge, rolled ~60 deg + 3D tilt, unrolls/shrinks with a strong ease-out and
  LANDS dead centre, perfectly flat and straight (20 frames); it never stays tilted and never moves aside; light bar through its centre, word types behind.
  The card lands SMALLER than the word (~315 px wide vs a ~840 px word at 370 px) so the word stays readable around it (Krish 2026-11-19).
  The card is SOLID dark (100 % opaque), never see-through (Krish 2026-11-19).
  Glitch blocks never sit on top of / touching type.
- Big numerals / words must read straight and centred (centre on the glyphs, not the layer box). No leftover tilt on anything that "lands".
- Halftone dot transition: Krish wants it kept exactly like the refs -- do not remove or change it.
- Glows are blurred on a padded layer (glow_screen) so they never show the layer's box as a rectangle.
- **Camera (Krish 2026-11-19, after v2: "almost 0 camera movement... add the same kind of camera movement we had in the documentry skill"):**
  speaker runs open punched in 1.20 and zoom out to 1.00 over 2.6 s on the user ease (0.68,0,0.03,1), anchored on the face, never below 1.0;
  then a push/pull on each key line; moves are stacked deltas (plan2.SPK_CAM), each next move starts ~40-60 % into the previous
  (keyframe overlapping) and lands before the cut. Graphics + B-roll get keyframed camera too (plan2.G_CAM: zoom-outs on entry,
  pushes onto the pay-off element, a slide on B2). Check with the per-frame speed print before rendering.
- **Element motion:** photos/cards/squares fly in from an offset + angle and LAND straight in place (fly_in, user ease), the panel rises,
  the '500' rises, the neon box grows in, the label rises, number rows slide. All graphics/B-roll render 4 sub-frames (180 deg shutter);
  random flicker (digits, glitch blocks, scramble) is pinned to the frame time so it doesn't smear.
- Caption columns clear the head even at 1.20 zoom (Ron cx 852 w 330, Kristina cx 270 w 350); lead lines wrap BALANCED (no stray one-word lines).
- **End tail** (Krish: last word got cut off): the reel never ends on the last syllable. Voice stops after the word's real end (40 ms fade before the next word), then a 0.6 s hold of the last frame with the camera still pushing, caption on, music fading (plan2 SPEECH_END / END_TAIL).
- Speaker shots that open < 0.3 s before a pause cut use the next piece's lead-in handle (no ghost blend right after the entry).
- Speaker grade: clean neutral (no warm push), sat 0.94, soft blacks. B-roll in colour, hard cuts. No B&W ending.
- Finish: graphics grain + vignette 0.30 + Texturelabs tex 0.35 + radial blur 0.5; speaker vignette 0.22, radial 0.35, no texture.

## The look (measured from the ref)
**Captions** (`scripts/jstyle.py`)
- Apple Garamond Light (`~/Library/Fonts/AppleGaramond-Light.ttf`, Light Italic for italics), white, ~100 px.
- **One word at a time** at its spoken time, centred x 540 on the chest (y ~1010 on Ron, ~980 on a second guest). Enters with a vertical Text Blur over 4 frames, soft shadow + faint glow.
- **Emphasis = two lines**: small lead word (~52 px) above a big main word (~112 px). Main word styles:
  - blue box (50,157,189), white text, wipes in from the left;
  - blue glow smear behind the word (for the feeling words: "contribution", "equalizer");
  - grey italic on the light-blue ground ("*solopreneur*", "*advantages*");
  - black box on the light ground ("500 companies.");
  - teal typewriter box (14,153,174) with a blinking cursor over a full-frame texture.
- Names, numbers and key words always go in the emphasis line, never in the single-word stream.

**Scenes** (alternate speaker / graphic every 2-5 s)
- **Speaker**: warm dark grade (R 1.07, B 0.86, gamma 1.12). Face held at y ~600, clear of the hook text. Last speaker shot = black & white.
- **Light-blue ground** (215,231,253): real cut-out objects (Gemini image → rembg isnet) drop in from above with vertical motion blur and land inside a dashed design-tool **selection box** with square corner handles (box appears just after the landing). A second object pushes the first aside. Pop SFX on landing. Dark text above.
- **Dark teal ground** (1,13,18): one glowing object rises in (Deep Glow = two blurs, teal-tinted screen), title word above, a small sentence builds word by word under the title. Slow push.
- **Texture**: full-frame texture (circuit board for AI) at 62% brightness, slow push + 2° turn, centre typewriter label; typing SFX per label.
- **B-roll run**: real stock video (Pexels portrait UHD, `pexels.com/download/video/<id>/` works with curl), B&W with halftone grain, gentle eased push, **hard cuts** between clips with a camera-shutter SFX, single words keep running centre frame.
- **Hook text** (when the script doc gives one): small spaced CAPS Apple Garamond 42 px at y 268, static first frame to last.

**Transitions**
- Blue-white **pixel transition** (`assets/pixel_transition_2.mov`, tinted, 0.6 s centred on the cut) on speaker ↔ graphic and into/out of the B-roll run; whoosh SFX peaking on the cut.
- Hard cuts elsewhere (B-roll clips, graphic → speaker in some places).
- Cuts inside the same person's footage (pauses removed): 5-frame eased cross-blend, never a jump.

**Camera** (user, 2026-11-18: "very smooth, no laggy or unnecessary motion, every move intentional")
- Each speaker shot gets **ONE move with a reason**, starting on the cut: pull back to reveal / introduce, lean in on a personal or key line, slow push across a serious sentence. Fast ease-out (~1 s) then near-still (1.2 % drift).
- Consecutive shots of the same person **continue the zoom** (next shot starts at the previous end zoom) so nothing pops.
- Motion blur from sub-frame camera samples (180° shutter) on every speaker move.
- Graphics: slow eased pushes only; objects bring their own motion.

**Finish** (`scripts/jfinish.py`): radial fast blur + chromatic aberration + vignette + Texturelabs Grunge 356M luminance texture, per scene: light grounds very light (vig 0.10, tex 0.45), dark/texture medium, speaker/B-roll full.

**Audio** (`scripts/mix.py`): voice from the cleanest camera, crossfaded joins → **Adobe Podcast Enhance v2** (podcast.adobe.com/en/enhance in neo, "Download separate speech track") → -14 LUFS; instrumental bed (screened with Whisper for lyrics) at -37 LUFS with fades; SFX: whooshes on pixel transitions, pops on landings, typing on labels, shutter on B-roll cuts; loudnorm -14 / TP -1.5 + limiter.

## Building a reel
1. `edl.py`: cut the script pieces (camera seconds), energy-based pause cutting against room tone, fillers out → `edl.json`, `words_rec.json`.
2. `plan.py`: SHOTS (speaker moves with their reason), PX transitions, WORDS / EMPH / graphic text timed to the words.
3. Assets: Gemini images + rembg cut-outs in `assets/gen/`, B-roll in `broll/use/` (cut to 9:16, 29.97, all-intra).
4. Cache speaker pieces as all-intra files (`src/pieces/pNN.mp4`, 0.5 s handles) for fast exact seeks.
5. Stills first: `render.py test t1 t2 ...` → contact sheet → user. **Ask before rendering video.**
6. `mix.py`, then `render.py full out.mp4` (9 parallel chunks + concat + mux), `open` it.

## v3 rules (Krish notes on v2, 2026-11-19) — override anything above
- **Animations must MEAN what is said.** The refs set the LOOK (fonts, ground, glow, neon, halftone); the animation itself is ours and must illustrate the line (e.g. "same advantages" = small-business owners + advantage chips that check in; "Fortune 500 companies" = real Fortune 500 logos; "solopreneur" = one woman + the hats she wears). Never drop in ref vocabulary that has no meaning (old panel + progress bar + gradient squares, tower/shop cards were rejected).
- **Never stock footage.** B-roll = real footage of the speaker's own company (Ron: Fox 40 floor from "How Ron Foxcroft built Fox 40 International | The Entrepreneurs", YouTube IAhWRuhmJ4k, via y2meta) shown as framed video cards on the tech ground, or real photos (Pinterest). Same picture never repeats in another scene.
- **Pictures slide in** (user ease, from off-screen, land straight) with NO motion blur. Graphics render without sub-frame blur.
- **Captions on speakers appear normally**: plain 3-frame fade per word, no slide/blur/stretch, no exit — a phrase stays until the next one replaces it. Placement varies (chest / left / beside head), never on a face: `facecheck.py` (YuNet face detector) must report 0 overlaps before rendering.
- **Alignment follows the side (GLOBAL memory rule edit-rule-text-alignment-by-side):** left-placed text left-aligned, right-placed right-aligned, middle centred; `caption_block` derives it from cx.
- **Shadows on ALL text** (`drop_shadow` / `text_sh`).
- **No hook title** ("AI IS THE GREAT EQUALIZER" was rejected; only add one if Krish asks).
- **No B&W flash** on graphic -> speaker; clean cut + the speaker zoom-out.
- **Halftone stays exactly the same look but fast: 0.30 s.** Graphic -> graphic = zoom-through dissolve (0.40 s), never a bare cut.
- Typed words: the **cursor blinks** (~1 Hz) once typed.
- Numbers **count up** (500: 0 -> 500 in 1.1 s, glow swells as it lands).
- **Neon box opening is long and smooth** (1.0 s: grows 0.86 -> 1 on the user ease, border traces round, glow builds, text types after 35 %); glow canvas padded so it never cuts off.
- Code card: rotation transition lands over 40 frames, then the **code keeps running** inside (typing, highlight bar, output lines).
- Big word reveal option: **glowing pixel wipe** (`pixel_wipe`).
- Logo / image moments = **Pinterest image-trail, measured frame by frame (refs_jen2/pin/all, 302 frames)**: a hidden cursor sweeps, pauses, sweeps back and stops; a card POPS at full size on top every ~2 frames (each ~62-85 px of cursor travel), never while the cursor rests; max ~8-9 visible, the OLDEST fades to black over 3 frames; cards small (14-22 % of width), mixed landscape/portrait/square, radius ~9 px, no border, no shadow, no label; content fills the card. (`trail_spawns`, `g1c` in render3.py; logos = simple-icons SVG -> resvg-py.) Ron 02: Krish asked for the trail to go round a CIRCLE and end as a full ring of 12 logos (r 300, centre 540,1100, none fade) and for SQUARE corners on logo cards (no roundness). Then (2026-11-19) replaced by the **revolving ring** from IG DY9YjEVgOCz (refs_jen2/revolve): all 12 cards in one tight overlapping ring that REVOLVES round its centre, cards stay upright facing camera, ring tilted in 3D (perspective, far side smaller, near on top), whips in on graph 1 (-230 deg, tilt 50->16 deg) with 180-deg-shutter motion blur, then keeps turning ~24 deg/s; `_rev_state`/`_rev_cards`/`g1c` in render3.py.
- PNG hero moment = **Trailer 1 'Alabama' reveal = a GLOWING PIXEL WIPE, top -> bottom** (NOT a flip; Krish corrected v3): `pixel_wipe_down` - ~0.38 s, square pixels switch on in a band at the leading edge, land white-hot and cool to real colour in ~3 frames, whole object glows white-blue and the glow dies ~0.6 s after; the object grows 0.88 -> 1 and drifts into place; huge dark ghost silhouette behind; giant faint word scrolling. Solopreneur PNG = pin/bw_11.jpg cut out (laptop mask fixed by polygon), bottom edge faded. Review single animations with `clip3.py t0 t1 out.mp4`.

"""Jennifer-style stills rendered with the skill's own engine (scripts2/jstyle2.py).
  python jen_stills.py tools
"""
import os, sys
import numpy as np, cv2
from PIL import Image
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/skills/jennifer-musselman-style/scripts2'))
import jstyle2 as J

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, 'stills')


def finish(img, seed=0, vig=0.30):
    """graphics finish from the skill: grain + vignette"""
    img = J.grain(img, 5.0, seed)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:J.H, 0:J.W].astype(np.float32)
    r = np.sqrt(((xx - J.W / 2) / (J.W * 0.62)) ** 2 + ((yy - J.H / 2) / (J.H * 0.55)) ** 2)
    img = img * (1 - vig * np.clip(r - 0.35, 0, 1) ** 1.4)[..., None]
    return np.clip(img, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


def save(img, name):
    p = os.path.join(OUT, name + '.png')
    Image.fromarray(finish(img)).save(p)
    print('rendered', p)

def persp(rgba, yaw=0.0, pitch=0.0, roll=0.0, z=1.0, f=1400):
    """3D rotate a flat card (degrees) and return a premultiplied RGBA on a padded canvas"""
    h, w = rgba.shape[:2]; P = max(w, h)
    pts = np.float32([[-w/2, -h/2, 0], [w/2, -h/2, 0], [w/2, h/2, 0], [-w/2, h/2, 0]])
    a, b, c = np.radians([pitch, yaw, roll])
    Rx = np.array([[1, 0, 0], [0, math.cos(a), -math.sin(a)], [0, math.sin(a), math.cos(a)]])
    Ry = np.array([[math.cos(b), 0, math.sin(b)], [0, 1, 0], [-math.sin(b), 0, math.cos(b)]])
    Rz = np.array([[math.cos(c), -math.sin(c), 0], [math.sin(c), math.cos(c), 0], [0, 0, 1]])
    q = pts@(Rz@Ry@Rx).T; q[:, 2] += f
    proj = np.float32([[p[0]*f/p[2]*z+P, p[1]*f/p[2]*z+P] for p in q])
    M = cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(np.float32([[0, 0], [w, 0], [w, h], [0, h]]), proj)
    return cv2.warpPerspective(rgba, M, (2*P, 2*P), flags=cv2.INTER_LINEAR), P

    """flickering grey rectangles (ref r1 12.5-15.5), re-rolled every `rate` frames"""
    rng = random.Random(seed*31+int(_rt(t)*FPS/rate))
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = zone or (0, 300, W, H-300)

        x, y = rng.randint(x0, x1-w)//40*40, rng.randint(y0, y1-h)//40*40

def over(dst, src, x, y, op=1.0):
    """premultiplied src (h,w,4 floats 0-1) over dst (H,W,3 floats 0-255) at top-left x,y"""
    if op <= 0.001: return
    h, w = src.shape[:2]; x, y = int(round(x)), int(round(y))
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(0, x), max(0, y), min(dst.shape[1], x+w), min(dst.shape[0], y+h)
    if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0: return
    s = src[y0-y:y1-y, x0-x:x1-x]*op
    dst[y0:y1, x0:x1] = dst[y0:y1, x0:x1]*(1-s[..., 3:4])+s[..., :3]*255
def screen(dst, src_rgb, x=0, y=0):
    h, w = src_rgb.shape[:2]; x, y = int(x), int(y)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(0, x), max(0, y), min(dst.shape[1], x+w), min(dst.shape[0], y+h)
    if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0: return
    s = np.clip(src_rgb[y0-y:y1-y, x0-x:x1-x], 0, 255)
    dst[y0:y1, x0:x1] = 255-(255-dst[y0:y1, x0:x1])*(255-s)/255
def glow_screen(dst, rgb, sigma, gain, x, y):
    """soft glow of a layer, padded by 3 sigma so it fades out instead of being cut off at the layer's box"""
    p = int(sigma*3)+2
    g = cv2.GaussianBlur(np.pad(rgb, ((p, p), (p, p), (0, 0))), (0, 0), sigma)*gain
    screen(dst, g, x-p, y-p)

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**

   **Engines.**
   - jstyle3 (J3, ~/.claude/skills/jennifer-musselman-style/scripts3/jstyle3.py) and jstyle2 (J), both set to 1920x1080 by importing jen_stills_h (`J.W, J.H, J3.W, J3.H = 1920, 1080`).
   - Key J3 functions:
     - caption_block(dst, t, ph, cx, base_y, maxw, align): **pass align explicitly**; the auto thresholds are for 1080 width.
     - neon_box(dst, t, t0, txt, cx, cy, px, dur=1.0, type_rate=1.6): typing starts at t0 + dur*0.35.
     - _line_layout(words, px) → (lay[(t, w, rg, asc, x)], width); _put_word(dst, rg, asc, x, base_y, (op, 0, 0, 0), shadow, glow).
     - text_rgba(txt, px, face, fill, hs=1.15): hs=1.0 gives natural condensed Instrument Serif.
     - pop_in, pixel_wipe_down, halftone(a, b, k), TechBG(seed).render(t, amount), number_row, binary_strip.
     - glitch_blocks (zone height must be ≥ 240).
     - grain; EASE_USER (0.68, 0, 0.03, 1), EASE_G1_OUT (fast→slow, incoming), EASE_G2_IN (slow→fast, outgoing), EASE_IO, EASE_OUT3.
     - RNG_T pinning.

   **Transitions:**
   - Halftone 0.30 s (speaker ↔ graphic).
   - Zoom-through 0.40 s: the outgoing zooms 1.0→1.30 on G2 with a 2-frame dissolve; the incoming g1 zoom-in.
   - Pixel overlay ('/Users/gourav/Downloads/(Footage)/pixel transition 2.mov' recoloured via PX_RAMP, 14/24 s).

   **Rules and finishing:**
   - Same-person pause cuts use a 5-frame blend.
   - Sub-frame camera motion blur on speaker moves.
   - Finish: speaker vig 0.22 rb 0.35 tex 0; graphics grain 4.5 + vig 0.30 tex 0.35 rb 0.5; pre-finished stills ('pre') vig 0 tex 0.2 rb 0.35.

   **Safe zone (search result):**
   - SMPTE ST 2046-1: title safe 90% (5% margin/side → x 96–1824, y 54–1026), action safe 93% (3.5%/side). Netflix recommends the same. Legacy 80% title / 90% action.
   - Plan: draw all text in screen space after camera moves, and keep every text bbox inside title safe.
   - Sources to cite to the user:
     - https://pub.smpte.org/doc/st2046-1/20091123-pub/st2046-1-2009.pdf
     - https://backlothelp.netflix.com/hc/en-us/articles/4406208331923-Title-Safe-and-Safe-Action-Best-Practices
     - https://Www.Wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_safe

   **Trailer 1 typography (0:41–end):**
   - Condensed light serif (≈ Instrument Serif at natural width), white, large (~120–130 px at 1080p).
   - Very tight leading (~0.92 em); words appear one by one, stacked.
   - The key word on a solid colour box (violet in the ref → use our teal→blue gradient/blue).
   - Sometimes the last line sits on a dark translucent box; soft shadow.

   **Recording YouTube in neo:**
   - MediaRecorder on `video.captureStream(30)`, vp9 30 Mbps, anchor download to ~/Downloads, then convert to all-intra 29.97 mp4.
   - Seek with the 'seeked' event.
   - Skip ads: snapshot, find `button "Skip" [ref=eN]` (not "Skip navigation"), page.click(ref).
   - Scan sheets: an in-page canvas tile of seeks.

   **Other:**
   - Eye-pair similarity alignment for match cuts: cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D of the two eye points → (BW/2 ± IOD/2, EY).
   - Wikimedia Commons API (generator=search, iiurlwidth=1800) with a generic UA; rate limit 429.
   - Audio: voice highpass 85 + afftdn → -14 LUFS; music kulakovka at -37 LUFS (from 20 s); SFX by peak dB; two-pass loudnorm -14/TP -1.5 + alimiter; Whisper listen-check.

def night_grade(img):
    """red-lit night B-roll into the reel palette: colour mostly out, shadows deep blue, screen-lit highlights cool white"""
    img = img * 1.35
    g = img.mean(2, keepdims=True)
    img = g + (img - g) * 0.26
    l = np.clip(g / 255, 0, 1)
    w = np.clip(1 - l / 0.55, 0, 1) ** 1.2
    img = img * (1 - 0.55 * w) + np.array((6, 30, 80), np.float32) * 0.55 * w
    img = img + (np.array((225, 240, 255), np.float32) - img) * 0.12 * np.clip((l - 0.4) / 0.6, 0, 1)
    return np.clip((img - 110) * 1.12 + 112, 0, 255)

- **Safe zone:** every text now sits inside the 90% title-safe area of the frame (the standard trailer rule), and camera zooms can no longer push it out.
  - Sources: [SMPTE ST 2046-1](https://pub.smpte.org/doc/st2046-1/20091123-pub/st2046-1-2009.pdf), [Netflix title safe guide](https://backlothelp.netflix.com/hc/en-us/articles/4406208331923-Title-Safe-and-Safe-Action-Best-Practices), [Title safe on Wikipedia](https://Www.Wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_safe).
- **02:** Lisa Su is now close and centred (AMD keynote at 25:22).
- **03:** "powered by" is removed and the WomenUp wordmark is centred in the bar.
- **04:** the photo is hidden until the card tears, then a quick shake hits on the tear.
- **05:**
  - The box keeps zooming in from the moment it appears until it leaves.
  - One red highlighter runs slower across the same headline line in three articles: [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2024/8/17/elon-musks-x-to-shut-operations-in-brazil-amid-bitter-legal-fight), [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/social-media/x-is-closing-its-operations-in-brazil-immediately-but-its-service-will-remain-live-for-users-165224020.html) and [SCMP](https://www.scmp.com/news/world/americas/article/3274924/elon-musk-closes-x-office-brazil-after-legal-dispute-judge).
  - Founders are 14 faces with the eyes locked in one spot, cutting every 0.2 s.
  - "leaders" now stays on screen for about a second.
  - At 13.3 s only the box slides out while the text stays, then the next scene slides in.
- **06a:** the text is bigger, on dark boxes.
- **15 s:** the pixel overlay is gone.
- **06c:** Fei-Fei plays as video with no box behind the caption, and a halftone takes it to the next scene.
- **07:** "Power" has no white glow, and the wheel is centred.
- **09:**

- **10a:** she's about twice as close, the grade is a vibrant blue, and "sparked" is very large in the gradient with no box.
- **10b:** only "lean in." shows, big, on her right, with the pixel overlay after it.
- **12:** the logo is centred.
- **Camera:** moves are slower and overlap each other, while the cuts stay fast.
